Two apps, built by hand

One codebase, both phones

Details

One codebase, both phones

What you get
One codebase builds each feature once for both phones, and a branded app is set up and built from the admin, with a guided checklist for the store steps.
Good to know
Releases are still made per platform, one for each store. Ten of the checklist's eighteen steps are still done by hand in the stores' own portals.

Straight into the event

You asked

“Let visitors into the event the moment they open the app.”

We delivered

In the event first. The data follows.

The current app

Waits on a full-screen download until everything has loaded.

The new app

Opens the event, then fills it in while you look around.

An illustration of the order things happen in, not a timing. Going straight in is switched on per app.

Being finished

Straight into the event, the first time

Details

Straight into the event, the first time

What you get
The first time visitors open an event they go straight in, and the event fills in behind them while they use the app.
Before
In the current app they waited on a full-screen download until the event, their own data and the list of people had all loaded, with no way to skip it.
Where it stands
Built and tested, and still being refined. What you see can change before it reaches your phones.
Good to know
Going straight in is switched on per app. With it off, the first entry still has a loading screen, and its bar moves as the data arrives. An event that asks visitors to sign in still asks for that first.

See how far set-up has got

Details

See how far set-up has got

What you get
While the event sets up, the home screen shows how far it has got and what it is doing now, the bar moves as the data arrives and never goes backwards, and each list says it is still filling until it is complete.
Before
In the current app one bar moved only when a whole step had finished.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
The set-up card on the home screen comes with going straight in and with the new home screen, both switched on per app. With them off, the loading screen's bar moves the same way, as the data arrives.

Being finished

Signal drops during set-up? It carries on after

Details

Signal drops during set-up? It carries on after

What you get
If the signal drops while the event is setting up, set-up pauses and says so, keeps what has already arrived, and carries on by itself when the signal returns.
Before
In the current app the set-up failed, showed a countdown and started again.
Where it stands
Built and tested, and still being refined. What you see can change before it reaches your phones.
Good to know
Set-up carries on by itself while the app is open; if the app is closed, set-up starts again the next time it is opened. If set-up fails for another reason, it offers to try again; what is saved is kept, and the event's content is downloaded again.

Being finished

Up to date, and says so when it cannot be

Details

Up to date, and says so when it cannot be

What you get
After set-up the app refreshes on a timer, every time you come back to it, when a notification arrives while it is open or is tapped, and when you pull down on a list.
Before
The current app refreshed on a timer and after changes, notifications included, but not when you came back to it, and pulling down did not fetch the event's data again.
Where it stands
Built and tested, and still being refined. What you see can change before it reaches your phones.
Good to know
If the app cannot reach the platform it keeps showing what it has, says it is showing saved data and when it last updated, and offers a refresh. With no internet at all it says so.

Being finished

Each event arrives as one ready-made package

Details

Each event arrives as one ready-made package

What you get
The new app's connection to the platform prepares each event as one ready-made package in each of the event's languages; the app adds it to the phone without touching the visitor's own data, then fetches only what changed since.
Before
The current app used a package only where it was switched on for an event, and swapped its whole database for it while the visitor waited on the loading screen.
Where it stands
Built and tested, and still being refined. What you see can change before it reaches your phones.
Good to know
If there is no package or anything goes wrong, the app downloads the event the normal way. Where an app lets visitors straight into the event, this happens while they are already inside; otherwise it happens behind the loading screen.

You asked

“Keep the app working where the signal drops.”

We delivered

Works where the signal doesn't.

24h message or meeting reply waits for a signal before it is marked not sent, for you to retry

Act with no signal; it goes out when you reconnect

Details

Act with no signal; it goes out when you reconnect

What you get
You can scan a badge, take notes, rate, favourite, request meetings and send messages with no signal, and they go out when you are back online.
Before
The current app mostly read with no signal: it kept offline scans and re-sent them only at its next launch, and notes, ratings and messages made with no signal were refused or failed silently.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
Sending happens while the app is open and the signal returns; nothing is sent while the app is closed or in the background. Messages and meeting replies wait up to 24 hours for a signal, then are marked not sent for you to retry; scans and notes have no time limit. Editing your profile still needs a signal. Reopened fully with no signal, the menu may be empty until the signal returns.

News on its own page, readable with no signal

Details

News on its own page, readable with no signal

What you get
Event and exhibitor news has its own page in the app, with search, filters and full articles, readable with no signal.
Before
In the current app news was a web page that people could not really use.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
News appears once it is added to your event's menu. Articles are kept on the phone, so a new article appears after the app's next refresh.

You asked

“Help people find anything, then find their way to it.”

We delivered

One search box. Then the map takes you there.

7 kinds of content in one search box, grouped by kind

One search box for the whole event

Details

One search box for the whole event

What you get
One search box across the whole event (exhibitors, products, brands, sessions, speakers, people and buyers) that answers from the phone, even with no signal.
Before
In the current app each list searched only itself.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
The search box comes with the new home screen, switched on per app; without the home screen the app searches each list on its own. It sits on the home screen, not on your custom pages, and results come grouped by kind. A category name is not a search target, and a session does not return its linked exhibitors. New content appears after the app's next refresh.

Stand numbers that open the right map

Details

Stand numbers that open the right map

What you get
A stand number opens the floor plan at that stand when your event's menu has a floor plan; otherwise it is plain text, with no dead end.
Before
In the current app a stand number always tried to open the floor plan, even when the event had none to show.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
Stand numbers link to the plan whenever your event menu has a floor plan; there is no separate switch to turn the links off while keeping the plan. For events whose only plan comes from an outside provider, we have not checked this yet.

Filter the floor plan by exhibitor category

Details

Filter the floor plan by exhibitor category

What you get
Pick one of your exhibitor categories and the floor plan lights up every stand of every company in it, on the ExpoFP plan as well as on the app's own drawn plan, and zooms to where they are.
Before
The current app's ExpoFP screen had a name search only, with no category filter of its own.

Fully tested on the app's own drawn plan; the highlight on the ExpoFP plan is still being checked on phones. Ordering exhibitors by your tags, and sending tags to ExpoFP, is separate platform work.

Floor plan on the phone from the start

Details

Floor plan on the phone from the start

What you get
The whole floor plan is downloaded to your phone as soon as you open the event, kept up to date, and opens with no signal.
Before
The current app prepared the plan at launch, re-checked it once per visit to the tab, and with no saved copy could spin without end.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
Your own position on the plan is not shown yet.

Walks, not just routes

Details

Walks, not just routes

What you get
You pick the stands you want to see and let the map plan one walk through them, saved on your account.
Before
The current app drew a route between two points, and routes were not saved.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
A walk starts from the first stand you pick, not from where you stand. The map draws the walk and its stops; it does not talk you through the hall.

Any wording, changed without a store release

Details

Any wording, changed without a store release

What you get
Any wording in the app is changed for your app alone or for every app, with no store release, and phones in use pick it up within about half an hour.
Before
The current app could also take wording from the server; what is new is that any label, for one app or for all, is edited in one place and reaches phones in use without a release.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
The change is made in the admin and reaches phones in use within about half an hour; a closed phone gets it the next time it opens. It is per app, not per event, and it does not change the web portal's wording.

Native pages and your own menu, no store release

Details

Native pages and your own menu, no store release

What you get
The event's own pages are built into the app rather than shown as web pages, and the menu is reshaped from the new admin; phones pick the change up on their next refresh, with no store release.
Before
The current app's menu already came from the server, and its custom pages were web pages shown inside the app.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
Page and menu changes are made in the admin and reach phones on their next refresh. The new home screen is separate from this, switched on per app, and your pages open from the menu without it. The phone's home-screen widgets need a new build of your app.

Every open of a push, counted

Details

Every open of a push, counted

What you get
For pushes sent from the new admin, every open is counted, including pushes with no link, and sent, received, opened and failed are shown for each push.
Before
The current app counted a tap only when the push carried a link, and gave no open count per push.
Where it stands
Built and tested. We show it to you on a test event.
Good to know
Counts cover pushes sent from the new admin. Pushes sent the current way are counted the current way: a tap counts only when the push carries a link.

One look for the whole app, set in the admin

Details

One look for the whole app, set in the admin

What you get
One look is picked for the whole app in the admin and saved; installed apps take it the next time they open, with no app release. A look changes how screens are laid out; your colours and fonts stay your own, and each screen keeps the same information.
Before
The current app had one layout for every app; colours, fonts, logo and menu could be changed from the platform, never how a screen was laid out.

There are three new looks beside the one the app had: two main ones, and a third that builds on the second. Where a look has no drawing of its own for a screen, that screen is shown in the look it builds on. One look per app, not per event.
